title: the board replaces itself with merged code when it is idle: a secret-only drain refuses while a merge or an answer is in flight, writes answer 503 while draining, and only a session-owned board is stopped
acceptance: Why. T-203 (merged 2026-10-05) left the board notice-only: when `board_start` (bin/fm-herdr.py:2365-2421) reuses a verified board whose recorded `code` (board.json, the HEAD:board and HEAD:i18n tree ids from `board_code_id`, :2340-2353) differs from the clean checkout's, it records `stale: true` and a bilingual `stale_reason` telling the captain to stop the board and run `fm board` by hand (:2409-2416), and design §11 'Managed session defaults' (design/design.md:2748-2756) names automatic replacement as a separate follow-up because it must first make running merges, dispatches and send-back answers safe. Today firstmate restarts the board by hand after every board change (T-192, T-198, T-202 on 2026-10-05). The hazards, from T-203's preflight rounds: a `dispatch` answer awaits `fm-dispatch.sh`, spawned with `Bun.spawn` in the board's own process group (board/server.ts:1751-1762, awaited in the `/decisions` handler at :2250), so killing the board kills a dispatch in progress; a merge or send-back is started through `startOwned` with `keep --pid OWNER` (:1554-1558, :1764-1790) and survives only when the board is session-owned (`OWNER` is FM_SESSION_PID, :1553; a hand-started board owns them itself, design table at :2800); and an answer that arrives between a check and the stop must not be half-written.

Drain route in board/server.ts. Add `POST /drain`, a writing route with every rule of §8 'Who may write' (design.md:2209-2217, `writeRefusal`, server.ts:1939-1944: credential, Origin, JSON) plus one more: the bearer must be the secret itself, never the tab token (compare with `same(m[1], SECRET)`; a page cannot drain the board). Body `{}` asks to drain; body `{"release": true}` releases. Module state: `let draining = 0` (the ms it was set, 0 when not draining) and `let effectsInFlight = 0`. A drain request answers, without writing anything: 409 `{error, code: 'drainBusy', busy: 'merge'}` when any decision record in any project has `mergeOf(d) === 'running'` (readResponses, :640-660; this includes merges started by an earlier board and recovered by `recover`, :1815-1845); 409 `{..., busy: 'answer'}` when `effectsInFlight > 0`; otherwise it sets `draining = Date.now()` and answers 200 `{draining: true, pid: process.pid, session_owned: <true when process.env.FM_SESSION_PID matches /^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$/>, owner: <that FM_SESSION_PID as a number, or null>, started: STARTED}` (STARTED is set at :2403). The check and the set run with no await in between, so no answer can slip in. A release sets `draining = 0` and answers 200 `{draining: false}`. A drain left set for 30 s without the board exiting is released by the board itself (checked on each request and by a 1 s timer like the one at :1847), so a crashed caller never leaves the board refusing writes.

Answers count while they run, and nothing is written while draining. In the `POST /decisions` handler (:2159-2283), `effectsInFlight` is incremented after `writeRefusal` passes and before the body is parsed, and decremented in a `finally` around the whole `req.json().then(...)` chain, so it spans the record creation, every effect including the awaited `dispatchTask` (until fm-dispatch.sh exits or its 60 s timer kills it) and `sendBack`'s 3 s start check, and the decision_made emit. `POST /tasks` (:2290) and `POST /open` (:2364) do the same (their work is synchronous today; the counter keeps that true if it changes). While `draining` is set, each of the three routes answers 503 `{error: 'the board is restarting; send it again in a moment', code: 'boardRestarting'}` right after `writeRefusal` and before anything is read, written, emitted or spawned (a write that already passed the check finishes; the drain waited for it). A send-back worker round and a merge helper are session-owned and outlive the board, so they are not counted after their handler returns: exactly today's ownership rule, unchanged. i18n: add `boardRestarting` to i18n/ui.en.json ('not sent: the board is restarting with new code; send it again in a moment') and i18n/ui.zh-TW.json ('未送出：看板正在重新啟動，請稍後再送一次'); zh-CN is derived through i18n/tw2cn.tsv, which already maps every Traditional character in that string (啟, 動, 請, 後; the rest are shared), so no tw2cn.tsv row is needed. Also add `drainBusy`, the code of /drain's 409 answer: en 'the board was not restarted: a merge or an answer is in progress', zh-TW '看板未重新啟動：合併或回覆進行中' (every Traditional term in it is already in tw2cn.tsv: 啟, 動, 合併, 覆, 進行中). Both codes are written in server.ts as `code: "boardRestarting"` and `code: "drainBusy"` (double quotes, like `code: "mergeBusy"` at :2207), so tests/i18n.test.sh:49-66, which requires every code the server sends to be in both dictionaries, covers them; the page already shows `r.code` as a feedback key (board/public/index.html:801, :842), so no page code changes.

Replacement in bin/fm-herdr.py. Add `board_drain(url, port, release=False)`: a POST to `<url>/drain` with `Authorization: Bearer <board_secret(port)>` (board_secret, :2148), `Origin: <url>`, `Content-Type: application/json`, body `{}` or `{"release": true}`, timeout 5 s; it returns the parsed JSON for 200, the parsed JSON with `status: 409` for 409, and None for anything else (404 from a board that predates this task, 403, 503, OSError, no secret file) - it never raises. In `board_start`, on the reuse path and BEFORE `record` is built with `**board_open(url, port)` (:2399-2400), so that `board_open` runs exactly once per call, against whichever board survives, and no sign-in code is minted for a board about to be stopped, and only when the T-203 stale rule holds (reused, recorded `old` code present, `current` code present and not dirty, and not `board_same_code(old, current)`, :2409-2410): call `board_drain`. (a) None: keep today's notice exactly (`stale`, `stale_reason` with 'restart it by hand'), nothing else. (b) 409: keep the board; `stale: true` and `stale_reason` = {en: 'the board runs older code (<old> -> <new>); a merge or an answer is in progress, so it was not replaced; run fm board again when it ends', 'zh-TW': '看板仍在執行較舊的程式（<old> -> <new>）；有合併或回覆正在進行，所以沒有替換；結束後再執行一次 fm board'}. (c) 200 with `session_owned` false: release the drain, keep the board, and keep today's 'restart it by hand' notice (a hand-started board owns its merges and send-backs and is never stopped). (d) 200 with `session_owned` true: send SIGTERM to the reported `pid` only when it is an int > 1 and `os.kill(pid, 0)` succeeds; then wait up to 10 s, polling every 0.1 s, until `http_get(url)` raises an OSError that is not a `urllib.error.HTTPError` (port free; `http_get` re-raises HTTPError, :2120-2125, and HTTPError is an OSError subclass, so a board still answering 5xx while it shuts down counts as occupied, exactly as the fresh-start path treats it at :2378-2380); if the port frees, continue into the fresh-start path above (the same occupied check, spawn and verify code as an unreused board: one implementation, factored into a local helper rather than copied), then build `record` with the single `board_open` call and recompute `page_http_verified` (:2399) against the replacement board. Ownership: the replacement board is owned by the SAME session as the board it replaces, never by whoever ran this `fm` command: the fresh-start helper takes an `owner` argument, and case (d) passes the drained board's `owner` from the /drain answer when it is an int > 1 and `os.kill(owner, 0)` succeeds; only when that owner is gone does it fall back to `lifeline().session_owner()` (bin/fm-herdr.py:2385, the rule a fresh start uses today). So `fm board` from a short-lived terminal never moves a long-lived session's board (and the merges and send-backs it will start, server.ts:1553-1557) under that terminal. The reuse path also copies `owner` forward from the previous board.json into the record (today it is set only when not reused, :2405-2409), so board.json always names the board's owner, and the record carries `reused: false`, `code: current`, `owner`, and `replaced: {from: <old short code>, to: <new short code>}` with no `stale`; if it does not free in 10 s, or the pid check fails, call `board_drain(..., release=True)` and keep the board with `stale: true` and `stale_reason` = {en: 'the board runs older code (<old> -> <new>) and did not stop when asked; restart it by hand: stop the board process and run fm board', 'zh-TW': '看板仍在執行較舊的程式（<old> -> <new>），要求停止但沒有停下；請手動重啟：停止看板程序後執行 fm board'}. The whole sequence runs under the existing `.board.lock` (:2370), so two `fm` commands never replace one board twice. Nothing new is tried when the code is unknown, dirty or equal: those stay exactly as T-203 left them (no drain request at all).

Who triggers it. Both callers of `board_start` get it with no change of their own: `fm board` (main mode 'board', :2768-2781; exit 0 or 69 as today, plus 70 when `board_start` raises, as today; a replaced board prints one stderr line per language: 'fm board: replaced the board: <old> -> <new>' and 'fm board: 看板已換成新程式：<old> -> <new>', from a new `replaced_reason` dict in the record) and `fm-session.sh start` (report['board'], :2849). The autopilot does not call it (it never starts the board; a reloaded autopilot leaves the board to the next fm command). After a merge, firstmate's fast-forward of the engine checkout followed by any `fm board` or session start replaces the board when it is idle.

Tests (workers do not run them; evidence is the required GitHub check and the gates). (1) tests/session.test.sh `test_board_code_notice_uses_its_own_git_fixture` (:166-228) keeps every assertion and gains `patch.object(m, 'board_drain', return_value=None)` in its reused-board block, so its stale path is case (a) and `start.call_count == 0` and `kill.call_count == 0` still hold (the test must never reach a real board on 4173). New cases in the same file, same own-git-fixture pattern: (b) board_drain returns `{'status': 409, 'busy': 'merge'}` -> board kept, the 409 reason, no kill, no start; (c) 200 with `session_owned: False` -> one release call, the hand notice, no kill; (d) 200 with `session_owned: True` and a pid -> `os.kill(pid, SIGTERM)` once, http_get raising a plain OSError (URLError/ConnectionRefusedError, not HTTPError) after the kill, lifeline start called once with `owner` equal to the drained board's `owner` (not the test's session owner), `board_open` called exactly once, record `reused: False`, `code` equal to the current code, `replaced` present, no `stale`, and `fm board` stderr carries the two replaced lines; (d2) the port never frees -> release called, board kept, the 'did not stop' reason, `board_open` called once; (d5) the drained board's owner is not alive -> the replacement uses `lifeline().session_owner()`; (f) a reused board that is not stale keeps and records the previous `owner`; (d4) during the wait http_get raises `urllib.error.HTTPError` (503) a few times and then a plain OSError -> the HTTPErrors count as occupied (no early start), then the replacement completes; (d3) pid check fails (os.kill(pid, 0) raises) -> no SIGTERM, release, 'did not stop' reason; (e) equal, dirty or unknown code -> board_drain not called. (2) tests/board-card-effects.test.sh (the real bun server with stubs, :40-85): add a `wait-$task` file to the fm-dispatch.sh stub (loop with `sleep 0.1` until the file is removed, at most 30 s, then behave as today) and a `wait-merge` file to the fm-merge.sh stub (same loop before it emits merged); cases: POST /drain with the tab token -> 403, with the secret but no Origin -> 403; while a dispatch answer is held -> /drain 409 busy 'answer', then remove the file, the answer completes, /drain 200 with `pid` and `session_owned`; while draining, POST /decisions, /tasks and /open each answer 503 `boardRestarting` and no decision file, event or stub call is written; /drain with `{"release": true}` -> 200 and a later answer is accepted; while a merge is held -> /drain 409 busy 'merge'; a drain not followed by an exit is released after 30 s: an env override `FM_BOARD_DRAIN_TTL_MS`, read once at start, never longer than 30 000, as FM_BOARD_CODE_TTL_MS does (server.ts:1924); this one case starts its OWN second board with `FM_BOARD_DRAIN_TTL_MS=500`, using the suite's inline start pattern (tests/board-card-effects.test.sh:109-111: `FM_ROOT=<dir> FM_PORT=0 bun run <dir>/board/server.ts > <dir>/out 2>&1 < /dev/null &`, then `board_port <dir>/out <pid>` and the /api/state wait loop) on its own fixture directory made the same way as `$x` (copy of the engine files the suite already copies, its own stubs and its own state, no decisions), signed with `secret_of` for its port and stopped with `stop_pids` (tests/lib/board.sh) in the suite's cleanup; so the suite's main board keeps the 30 s default and the 503 and held-answer cases cannot be released under them. The suite's main board is started by tests/lib/board.sh with FM_* cleared, so it is not session-owned: its /drain 200 answers `session_owned: false`, which those cases assert. The existing assertions of that suite stay unchanged. (3) i18n: the new `boardRestarting` and `drainBusy` keys are in both dictionaries; tests/i18n.test.sh:13-14 (key parity) and :49-66 (every server code translated) need no change and stay green only because both keys are added. Stubs answer like the real scripts (fm-dispatch prints the task id it started and exits 0; fm-merge emits `merged`).

Docs, edited in place (T-189: nothing appended at the end of design.md): design §11 'Managed session defaults', the paragraph 'Board reuse is verified...' (design.md:2748-2756): replace the 'separate follow-up' sentences with the drain-and-replace rule (secret-only POST /drain, busy on a running merge or an answer in flight, 503 boardRestarting while draining, only a session-owned board is stopped, a hand-started board keeps the by-hand notice, a board that will not stop is released and named, the 30 s self-release); and the ownership table row for `board/server.ts`'s fm-merge.sh/fm-worker.sh (:2800) gains 'fm-dispatch.sh (dispatch answer): the board's own process group, which is why the board drains before it is replaced'. §8 'Who may write' (:2209-2217): add `POST /drain` to the list of writing routes and say it alone also requires the secret rather than the tab token. The usage text of `fm board` in bin/fm.sh (board usage, about :101-110) gains one line: a stale session-owned board is replaced when idle.

In flight. No stored record is migrated. board.json gains the optional `replaced` field and keeps `code`/`stale`/`stale_reason` as T-203 defined them. A board running pre-T-209 code has no /drain route: `board_drain` gets 404 and returns None, so the first `fm board` after this merges keeps it with today's by-hand notice; once the captain restarts it by hand (or it is restarted for any other reason), every later board change is replaced automatically. Merges and send-backs in flight are untouched (a drain refuses while one runs). Workers do not run the suites; evidence is the required check and the gates.
